title: Mexico's Pro Football League Gears Up for 2027: Gallos Negros Name Marco Martos Head Coach and a New Team Joins the LFA
excerpt: Gallos Negros de Querétaro unveiled a new identity and named veteran coach Marco Martos to lead them into the 2027 LFA season, while the Toros del Estado de México join as the league's eighth team — and the NFL returns to Mexico City on Sunday.
content:
Mexico's professional American football league is already building toward 2027. Gallos Negros de Querétaro presented a new visual identity, new uniforms and a new coaching staff for the 2027 season of the Liga de Fútbol Americano Profesional (LFA) on Nov. 12, before about 100 people at the Auditorio BLOQUE in Querétaro.

The centerpiece of the presentation was the naming of Marco Martos as head coach. Martos is one of Mexican football's most respected figures: a former player who coached the Leones Anáhuac Cancún from 2005 to 2018 and spent the last two seasons leading the Arcángeles de Puebla, the LFA expansion team he coached in 2025 and 2026. Querétaro mayor Felifer Macías and INDEREQ director Iridia Salazar Blanco attended the presentation.

The club also announced a community flag football tournament, the Torneo de Flag de Otoño-Invierno, running Nov. 21-27 at the Unidad Deportiva Josefa Ortiz de Domínguez in Querétaro, with 50 teams and 600 players taking part.

One day earlier, the LFA officially welcomed its newest franchise. The Toros del Estado de México were presented Nov. 11 as the league's eighth team for 2027, led by owners Fernando Fonseca and Federico Arreola. Simón Hernández will serve as the first head coach in team history, and Dominican offensive tackle Bayron Matos — a former NFL player — was announced as the Toros' first official signing. The team will train in the Santa Fe area, with its home stadium still to be announced.

The league played the 2026 season with seven teams, with the Caudillos de Chihuahua winning their third championship. The 2027 campaign, the LFA's tenth official tournament, is expected to kick off in February 2027.

The growth comes as American football's biggest stage returns to Mexico. The NFL plays in Mexico City on Sunday, Nov. 22, when the Minnesota Vikings face the San Francisco 49ers at Estadio Banorte — the league's first regular-season game in Mexico since 2022.

Monterrey's Osos, owned by NFL All-Pro Ryan Kalil and NBA All-Star Blake Griffin, also made news this week, announcing LIGHT Helmets as the team's first official partner. The Osos will take the field wearing the company's ultra-lightweight helmets, designed to reduce head and neck fatigue.
